title: Enforce role-scoped Photo visibility
evidence_required: FT-012-AC-001 and FT-012-AC-002 RED: no staff inventory list/visibility command currently enforces the accepted SPA/date/capture interval and photographer ownership, while the completed search/media/statistics seams only expose existing active-state behavior; GREEN: the exact authenticated API/UI filters persisted captured_at, denies foreign photographer or inaccessible scope, changes only is_active, excludes inactive Photos from new search and counters, preserves existing issued media, and restores without new processing; decisive comparison: fixed role/time fixtures inspect API results, Photo/media/face/state rows, search, counters and phone reads before delete, while inactive and after restore; artifact: focused redacted outputs under .tasks/TASK-107-T3-FT-012-W2/.
purpose: Expose the smallest role-safe inventory selection and visibility operation over the existing Photo model without adding a second deletion lifecycle.
success_outcome: Photographers can list and change only their own matching Photos, operator/developer can act within the accepted SPA scope, and soft-delete/restore changes only visibility while preserving stored and issued-session state.
anti_goals: Do not implement restore-all, hard purge, recent-statistics aggregation or worker behavior.
Do not add deletion history, tombstones, bulk-operation state, a Batch model or per-photo purge fields.
Do not mutate processing, Promo, Attempt, diagnostics or serving-control state.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL/MinIO, operator/default Photos and non-disposable staff sessions
Restore-all, hard-purge run/worker behavior and recent-statistics implementation
Direct writes to processing, promo, diagnostics or serving-control owner state
stop_conditions: Role-safe selection cannot use the existing principal, Photo fields and one-SPA access rules without a new authorization model.
Soft-delete or restore would require changing any field other than Photo.is_active or rebuilding issued sessions.
Verification cannot isolate all Photo/media/session fixtures and clean them without touching operator/default data.

constraints: Primary owner is inventory at src/face_moment/inventory/; HTTP remains a thin adapter and staff_access supplies only the principal.
Use the persisted effective captured_at and half-open selection interval; do not recalculate EXIF or introduce saved filters/pagination.
Use existing Photo.is_active as the only visibility marker and preserve all acceptance, processing and media fields.
Run authorization and state probes only against synthetic disposable users, Photos, objects and sessions.
invariants: A photographer never observes or mutates another photographer's Photo through this surface.
Inactive Photos do not enter new search/result formation or recent counters, while issued sessions may use existing media.
Restore preserves timestamps and processing state and creates no new upload or processing claim.
verification_targets: Exact API/HTML tests cover persisted capture-time filters, ordering, every role/ownership case, CSRF, idempotency and task-owned 401/403/404/422/5xx behavior; snapshot-conflict 409 belongs to TASK-110.
A disposable integration matrix compares Photo/media/face/state rows, exact compatible search, recent-counter eligibility and issued phone media before delete, while inactive and after restore.
Import/state inspection proves inventory owns authorization and visibility with no transport orchestration, foreign write or new lifecycle field.
